lean.fidelity_note: Both statements assert existence of smooth odd divergence-free data on $\mathbb T^3$ and a maximal smooth odd Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. The velocity is uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of the gradient and vorticity $L^\infty$ norms diverge. For every compact set away from the origin and every nonnegative integer $m$, both velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement represents torus fields by integer-periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$, uses essential suprema on the centered unit cube and the Euclidean operator norm for the gradient, and takes the derivative at time zero from the right. Pressure has zero spatial mean, as required in the paper’s conventions. It explicitly asserts that every maximal solution from the selected initial data has the same lifespan and velocity. This makes the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper precise. Neither statement imposes the Euler equations after $T_*$.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1
lean.plain: Finite-time singularity for smooth periodic Euler data
